## Summary

**Instrument built:** `tof_imaging` — a straight-line TOF imaging beamline:

| # | Component | Type | z (m, from src) | Key params |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | src | Source_simple | 0 | yheight=0.12, xwidth=0.1, dist=1.0, focus_xw/yh=ap_D, λ₀=lam, dλ=dlam, flux=1e13 |
| 2 | aperture | Slit (circular) | 1.0 | radius=0.5·ap_D |
| 3 | scraper | Slit (rect) | 10.0 | xwidth=yheight=0.3 |
| 4 | fov_mon | PSD_monitor | 20.0 | 128×128, 0.28×0.28 m, restore_neutron=1 |
| 5 | det | PSD_monitor | 25.0 | 256×256, 0.2×0.2 m, restore_neutron=1 |
| 6 | det_lam | L_monitor | 25.01 | 200 bins, Lmin=lam−2·dlam, Lmax=lam+2·dlam, restore_neutron=1 |

Parameters: lam=3.5 Å, dlam=1.3 Å, ap_D=0.016 m (all as instrument parameters, used exactly as specified with expressions like `0.5*ap_D`, `lam-2*dlam`, etc.)

**Run conditions:** seed=12345, gravity off (short 25 m path at 3.5 Å thermal-ish neutrons — gravity drop negligible over this range, consistent with archetype guidance but noted as a simplifying assumption).

**Final results (ncount=1×10⁸, seed=12345) — cross-checked against a 1×10⁶-ray run with same seed, consistent within statistics:**

| Monitor | Integrated Intensity I (n/s) | Error ± | Events (N) | Rel. err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fov_mon (PSD @ 20 m) | 1.1356×10¹⁰ | 9.52×10⁶ | 1,421,820 | 0.08% |
| det (PSD @ 25 m) | 3.6336×10⁹ | 5.39×10⁶ | 454,943 | 0.15% |
| det_lam (λ-monitor @ 25.01 m) | 3.6305×10⁹ | 5.38×10⁶ | 454,546 | 0.15% |

All monitors have >>1000 events and rel_err well below the 5% floor.

**Observations / sanity checks:**
- Beam is well-centered on all monitors (X0, Y0 ≈ 0, within a few mm — consistent with straight, unrotated geometry).
- Intensity drops ~3.1× between fov_mon (20 m) and det (25 m), consistent with the aperture-defined cone continuing to expand beyond the field-of-view monitor's larger acceptance (0.28 m) vs the detector's smaller area (0.2 m) — no anomalous >10× unexplained loss, so the transmission chain is geometrically sound.
- det and det_lam intensities agree to <0.1%, as expected since det_lam sits essentially at the same z (25.01 m) with the same aperture (0.2×0.2 m) and only records/filters by wavelength.
- det_lam wavelength distribution: center of mass = 3.500 Å, FWHM ≈ 2.60 Å, matching the specified lam=3.5 Å source with dlam=1.3 Å (flat distribution half-width, full width 2.6 Å) — confirms correct source/monitor wavelength binding.

**Assumptions disclosed:** flux value (1×10¹³ n/s/cm²/sr/Å) taken directly from the spec (arbitrary Source_simple normalization — absolute intensities scale linearly with this choice). No gravity applied since path (25 m) and wavelength (3.5 Å) are modest; if longer flight paths or colder neutrons were introduced, gravity should be re-enabled and rechecked.
